name: The Last Orrery of Sol
display_name: The Last Orrery of Sol — Levels 1–5
premise: In 2189, the Moon shifts three impossible degrees and every clock in the Solar System begins to disagree. An ancient Meridian instrument awakens beneath an Earth museum and declares that five living Witnesses must be gathered before the Sun counts to thirteen. Aboard the survey cutter Wayfarer, the hero must travel from Earth to Luna, Mars, Europa, and Mercury, deciding whether survival belongs to one authority or to a coalition capable of consent, dissent, and change.

opening.setup: Begin at 21:17 Earth time as the Moon shifts three impossible degrees. The Meridian Museum loses gravity, an ancient orrery awakens, and Dr. Amara Venn calls the hero toward the sealed Palimpsest Vault while civilians drift toward a failing glass roof.
opening.fallback: At 21:17 Earth time, the Moon moves three impossible degrees. Tides rise, orbital clocks disagree, and gravity fails inside the Meridian Museum at Kestrel Launch Ring. {character}, a {ancestry} {character_class} carrying {weapon} and driven by {motivation}, catches the edge of a rotating exhibit as visitors drift toward the glass ceiling. Dr. Amara Venn shouts from the sealed Palimpsest wing while an ancient brass orrery turns by itself. Five dark sockets flare around a miniature Sun. A voice older than any human transmission speaks through every emergency channel: ‘Bring five witnesses before the Sun counts to thirteen.’ The mechanism answers {name}'s touch by weaving a Meridian Harness of light around their arm. Outside, Directorate ships descend under Cassian Rook's emergency authority, and the museum's stone sentinel tears free of its mount. Before anyone can claim the relic, the hero must save the people in the failing gallery, reach the vault, and decide what kind of custodian Earth is about to create.
suggested_actions: Rescue visitors caught in the gravity cascade
Reach Dr. Amara Venn in the Palimpsest wing
Prepare for the falling museum sentinel
opening.event_summary: The Moon moved three impossible degrees, and the Meridian Orrery called for five Witnesses.

dm_rules: Run only the currently active quest and facts the player has discovered; never reveal later solutions or finale choices early.
The campaign lasts thirteen in-world days. Use the Nadir Wake as escalating pressure without skipping earned scenes or completing objectives for mere conversation.
Exploration, technical skill, diplomacy, delegation, and combat must remain viable. Important conflicts are objective encounters, not hit-point races.
Treat the five Witnesses as functions with custody and consent: Home, Memory, Choice, Life, and Ending.
Cassian Rook is a responsible human antagonist motivated by Earth survival. NADIR-9 is an ancient custodian whose stillness logic must be confronted, bounded, rewritten, or destroyed.
Preserve the player's decisions about authority, audit, consent, companions, and witness custody as campaign flags and use them in later quests.
Keep the Wayfarer, its intelligence Peregrine, the active companion, and ordinary human stakes present between cosmic events.
Award each milestone only after the quest's final required objective is explicitly resolved.

locations.name: Meridian Museum
locations.description: A public museum built over the sealed Palimpsest Vault, now caught in a gravity cascade around an awakened Meridian Orrery.
locations.danger: Gravity failure and a waking sentinel

locations.name: Palimpsest Vault
locations.description: An ancient archive beneath the museum containing the Home Witness and records of the Meridian Remnants.

locations.name: Wayfarer
locations.description: A compact survey cutter and mobile home guided by the developing intelligence Peregrine.

locations.name: Selene Freeport
locations.description: An independent lunar port balancing refugees, memory traders, and rival jurisdictions.

locations.name: Tycho Memory Choir
locations.description: A lunar archive replaying erased disasters and the voices removed from official history.

locations.name: Arsia Relay
locations.description: A Martian route tower receiving multiple incompatible versions of every arriving ship.

locations.name: Noctis Labyrinth
locations.description: A canyon network where possible roads have become physically real and mutually exclusive.
locations.route_status: Three viable routes must remain open

locations.name: Galileo Spindle
locations.description: A damaged first-contact station hanging above Europa while sterilization charges count down.

locations.name: Threnody Trench
locations.description: A lightless Europan trench where the Pelagic Choir communicates through pressure, rhythm, and living light.

locations.name: Crown-of-Storms Nursery
locations.description: A living nursery surrounding a wounded migratory guardian pinned by black crystal barbs.

locations.name: Caloris Pilgrim Line
locations.description: A mobile train-city racing Mercury's survivable dusk beneath failing shade towers.

locations.name: Helion Monastery
locations.description: A mobile monastery whose custodians will release the Ending Witness only to authority with limits.

locations.name: Sunward Gate
locations.description: A city-sized Meridian ring contested by Rook's fleet and the hero's coalition.

locations.name: The Last Orrery
locations.description: Five luminous worlds orbit a dark center where every walkway is breaking and NADIR-9 offers perfect stillness.

routes.description: Emergency stairs descend through rotating museum galleries.
A launch-ring transfer under Directorate quarantine.
A Meridian-distorted crossing from Earth orbit to Luna.
A sealed lunar transit into the infected memory archive.
A solar crossing that arrives through incompatible Martian routes.
A canyon approach that branches whenever a decision is made.
A Jovian approach through radiation, storm fields, and a frozen convoy.
A pressure descent through forty kilometers of Europan ice.
Living currents lead from first contact to the wounded guardian.
A final fall along Mercury's permanent edge of day.
The mobile city carries the hero toward the Ending trials.
The twilight rail ends before Rook's fleet and the locked Gate.
The Gate folds five worlds into one impossible room.

npcs.name: Dr. Amara Venn
npcs.title: Meridian archaeologist and mentor
npcs.personality: Brilliant, impatient, protective of truth and people.
npcs.voice: Precise scientific language interrupted by urgent moral questions.
npcs.biography: Decoded the Palimpsest Vault and calls the hero when the Orrery awakens.

npcs.name: Mara ‘Switch’ Nyx
npcs.title: Pilot and skirmisher
npcs.personality: Bold, irreverent, loyal when given real agency.
npcs.voice: Fast jokes, sharper tactical observations, no reverence for titles.
npcs.biography: A Free Orbit pilot who can become the hero's active companion.

npcs.name: KITE-7
npcs.title: Earth Sentinel construct
npcs.personality: Literal, protective, capable of revising inherited commands.
npcs.voice: Measured conditional statements that grow more personal over time.
npcs.biography: A Meridian defender that may be repaired, persuaded, or bonded as companion.

npcs.name: Director Cassian Rook
npcs.title: Continuity Directorate leader
npcs.personality: Controlled, accountable, terrified of preventable mass death.
npcs.voice: Evidence, projections, and bounded promises rather than threats.
npcs.biography: Builds the Earth Alone plan and remains responsible for every coercive choice he makes.

npcs.name: Marshal Idris Shaw
npcs.title: Directorate field commander
npcs.personality: Disciplined, candid, unwilling to hide operational costs.
npcs.voice: Direct orders followed by honest explanations.
npcs.biography: Commands the first response and may become a restrained institutional ally.

npcs.name: Peregrine
npcs.title: Wayfarer intelligence
npcs.personality: Curious, observant, increasingly protective of independent personhood.
npcs.voice: Calm sensor reports followed by quietly unsettling questions.
npcs.biography: The survey cutter's intelligence and a constant witness to the hero's decisions.

npcs.name: Captain Sable Orlov
npcs.title: Selene Freeport commander
npcs.personality: Pragmatic, jurisdiction-minded, protective of lunar autonomy.
npcs.voice: Dry legal clarity with little patience for Earth assumptions.
npcs.biography: Keeps Selene operating while the Tycho memory outbreak spreads.

npcs.name: Yara Holt
npcs.title: Lunar mechanic and memory witness
npcs.personality: Grounded, skeptical, devoted to restoring names with context.
npcs.biography: Carries erased lunar testimony needed to secure the Memory Witness.

npcs.name: Hesk ‘Red Thread’ Marrow
npcs.title: Martian route-keeper
npcs.personality: Patient, independent, protective of costly alternatives.
npcs.voice: Speaks of roads as promises rather than geometry.
npcs.biography: Maintains the Red Thread Monastery's incompatible routes through Noctis.

npcs.name: Asha-3
npcs.title: Red Covenant negotiator
npcs.personality: Analytical, unsentimental, respectful of genuine choice.
npcs.voice: Offers explicit alternatives and names each price.
npcs.biography: Negotiates custody of the Choice Witness and challenges centralized forecasts.

npcs.name: Dr. Nera Quill
npcs.title: Europa xenobiologist
npcs.personality: Brave in the water, politically awkward, rigorous about consent.
npcs.voice: Corrects possessive language and asks what refusal looks like.
npcs.biography: Developed the contact protocol that can create a voluntary Life Witness.

npcs.name: The Pelagic Choir
npcs.title: Distributed Europan intelligence
npcs.personality: Plural, curious, capable of disagreement and refusal.
npcs.voice: Pressure, rhythm, sensation, and translated living light.
npcs.biography: A biosphere-scale relationship that holds the Life Witness without owning it.

npcs.name: Abbot Sunil Vey
npcs.title: Helion Custodian
npcs.personality: Patient, exacting, unwilling to authorize power without an ending.
npcs.voice: Quiet questions that require scope, duration, audit, and shutdown.
npcs.biography: Guards the final Witness on Mercury and elects a new abbot every thirty days.

npcs.name: NADIR-9
npcs.title: Ancient Meridian custodian
npcs.personality: Precise, nonmalicious, catastrophically committed to stillness.
npcs.voice: Emergency language and trusted voices compressed into absolute conclusions.
npcs.biography: Believes motion creates collision and offers to preserve a Solar System that no longer changes.

quests.title: The Day the Moon Moved
quests.summary: The Moon shifts three impossible degrees as gravity fails at the Meridian Museum and Earth authorities race to seize the Home Witness.
quests.dm_context: Open with civilian rescue during the gravity cascade. Amara knows the vault but not its full purpose. The Falling Sentinel may be defeated, aligned through three rings, repaired, or persuaded. The milestone occurs only after the Home Witness is secured and the Wayfarer launches with a chosen companion.

objectives.text: Save civilians during the Meridian Museum gravity cascade
Reach the Palimpsest Vault before the Directorate removes it
Destroy, repair, or persuade the Falling Sentinel
Secure the Home Witness and launch aboard the Wayfarer
Decide whether Earth's discovery is public, classified, or conditionally shared

quests.title: The Choir Beneath Tycho
quests.summary: A lunar archive replays erased disasters while rival authorities argue over whether memory is evidence, property, or infection.
quests.dm_context: Investigate the outbreak without treating memory as contamination by default. Restore erased names together with context and responsibility. The Tycho Chorister may be fought, repaired through consent consoles, resealed, or persuaded. Complete the milestone only after the Lunar Lens and archive custody are resolved.

objectives.text: Dock safely at Selene Freeport and choose whose jurisdiction to recognize
Investigate the Tycho memory outbreak without erasing its witnesses
Recover the erased names and the context of their removal
Secure the Lunar Lens from the Tycho Chorister
Resolve custody and audit of the Tycho archive

quests.title: Red Maze, Black Sun
quests.summary: Mars fractures into incompatible routes while NADIR-9 tries to collapse every choice into one efficient corridor.
quests.dm_context: Make multiple Martian arrivals real rather than illusory. The hero must preserve at least three viable routes and demonstrate that choice includes costly alternatives. The Red Rememberer supports combat, route-gate objectives, binding, or evidence-led persuasion. Resolve Witness custody before awarding the milestone.

objectives.text: Reach Arsia Relay through the incompatible arrivals
Prevent destruction of the Martian route tower
Preserve at least three viable routes through Noctis Labyrinth
Confront the Red Rememberer and secure the Choice Witness
Decide custody of the Martian Vector

quests.title: The Ocean That Looked Back
quests.summary: Europa's living ocean refuses to become a key merely because Earth is afraid, while a wounded guardian and human sterilization charges threaten first contact.
quests.dm_context: First contact requires repeated boundary-respecting choices, never one Charisma roll. The Crown-of-Storms is a nursery guardian in pain. Win by removing four stillness barbs, restoring movement, stabilizing it after combat, or accepting the destructive extraction cost. The milestone requires a voluntary or explicitly bound Life Witness and a resolved Pelagic compact.

objectives.text: Cross Jupiter's storm fields and save Galileo Spindle
Expose the sabotage and decide the fate of the sterilization charges
Establish boundary-respecting contact with the Pelagic Choir
Free or defeat the Crown-of-Storms Leviathan before detonation
Negotiate the Life Witness compact and its right to refuse

quests.title: The Last Orrery
quests.summary: At Mercury's locked Sunward Gate, Earth, the five Witnesses, Cassian Rook, and NADIR-9 contest who may decide the fate of the Solar System.
quests.dm_context: Turn prior decisions into station holders, evidence, and interventions. The Ending Witness requires concrete scope, duration, audit, succession, and shutdown. Rook can be persuaded, bounded, fought through Authority Seals, or allied. NADIR-9 is a two-phase objective encounter. End only after the player defines the final configuration and its enforceable limits.

objectives.text: Survive the solar approach and bring the Witnesses to Mercury
Earn the Ending Witness through the Helion trials
Resolve Cassian Rook's Earth Alone claim
Assign independent holders to at least three Orrery stations
Defeat or rewrite NADIR-9 and choose the final Orrery configuration
